rules.description: Vi Mode: D as Trigger Key

rules.comment: This will disable Cmd + Shift + M in everye app unless you add the app id to the frontmost_application_unless block. Use `osascript -e 'id of app {APP_NAME}'` to determine the app name.
rules.description: Disable Cmd+M to minimize globally.

rules.comment: Workaround for a Colemak bug in the Claude app: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/68859. Note: the macOS Colemak input source re-translates Karabiner's output, so to send the app Cmd+K we emit key_code n (Colemak maps the n-position to 'k'). Digits are not remapped by Colemak, so Cmd+3 is emitted as-is.
rules.description: Claude: ⌘J → ⌘K, ⌘3 (New Session)

rules.comment: Opens the command palette and fires its first entry. key_code n is how the app is sent Cmd+K: it re-translates Karabiner's output through the macOS Colemak input source (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/68859), and physical n types 'k'. Enter follows with no hold -- untested, so if it ever fires the wrong palette entry, the palette had not finished opening and this wants a measured pause.
rules.description: Claude: ⌥N → New Chat (physical key j in Colemak)

rules.comment: Opens the project picker on the New Conversation screen by pressing it through the accessibility tree rather than clicking a hardcoded coordinate. The folder row is a local/cloud AXPopUpButton titled "Local", then the project picker, then a branch AXComboBox, a worktree checkbox and an AXButton described "Add another folder". Both popups carry nothing but an AXTitle of plain varying text, so no label tells them apart and --sibling cannot either -- they share a parent, and so do the Model, Effort and Usage popups further down, which is why the default reverse walk lands on Usage. Only their order separates them: --first --nth 2 is the second match in document order, the picker. The sibling that qualifies them is "Local", not "Add another folder": with no folder chosen the row is the Local popup and the picker and nothing else -- no branch combo, no worktree checkbox, no add button -- so a search qualified by "Add another folder" matched nothing at all there and the press did nothing (a run of found=false in ax-press.log, visited=523). The Local popup is in the row in both states and shares its parent, and it is itself match 1, so --nth 2 is still the picker; measured by --dry-run in both states, No folder and a chosen folder. It follows the toggle's label, so a row reading "Cloud" would need its own sibling. The coordinate this replaces was (315, 875); the picker measured (299,872 112x18) here, so the click was still landing, but only while the Claude window sat in its usual position and size, and it left the cursor sitting on the button. Logs one line per press to .claude/ax-press.log.
rules.description: Claude: ⌘P → Choose Project (physical key r in Colemak)

rules.comment: Clicks the Create PR button in the session view. The position is hardcoded, which the Electron renderer no longer forces: it does expose an accessibility tree, and the Cmd+P project-selector rule beside this one now presses its target through it. Converting this one means finding a discriminator for a button labelled "Create PR", and every dry run of that fires a PR. Coordinates are absolute on the main display; y matches the project-selector rule, x is the button's position in a 2x Retina screenshot (1313 px) halved to points. The cursor is left on the button rather than restored: restoring it needs a spawned script to read the cursor before Karabiner moves it, and the 200ms hold covering that read measured p50 101ms against a 300ms tail and one 963ms over 400 samples -- a race, not a margin. Dropping the restore removes the spawn, the hold and the race together. The 100ms warp-to-click gap stays: without it the click races the cursor move and the app registers only the hover, so the shortcut had to be pressed twice. Unlike the gap Cmd+P used to have, which measured 0, this one has not been driven to its floor -- the target is the Create PR button, so a binary search would fire it once per press.
rules.description: Claude: ⇧⌘P → Create PR (physical key r in Colemak)

rules.comment: Show Diff. The app ignores Cmd+Shift+D while the chat box has focus, so the rule first clicks an empty spot in the sidebar to blur it. Like the Cmd+Shift+P rule, the coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Claude window sits in its usual position and size. The cursor is left in the sidebar rather than restored: restoring it needs a spawned script to read the cursor before Karabiner moves it, and the 200ms hold covering that read measured p50 101ms against a 300ms tail and one 963ms over 400 samples -- a race, not a margin. Dropping the restore removes the spawn, the hold and the race together. Neither hold is needed: 0ms for both the warp-to-click gap and the click-to-keystroke gap opened the diff 10 times out of 10. The sidebar spot is always on screen, so the click races nothing, and the Cmd+Shift+D that follows is queued behind the click rather than competing with it -- the same reason the menu-bar sequences need no pauses. The expectation that the second gap was waiting on focus actually moving was wrong.
rules.description: Claude: ⇧⌘G → Show Diff

rules.comment: Opens the usage popover (the meter beside the composer) by pressing it through the accessibility tree rather than clicking a hardcoded coordinate. It is an AXPopUpButton whose AXDescription is the usage summary itself -- "Usage: Weekly · Fable: 64%, Resets Thu 1:00 PM, Context 129k / 1M (13%)" -- so the rule matches the stable "Usage: " prefix with the {} wildcard and lets the numbers vary. --role AXPopUpButton keeps it off the sidebar chat rows, whose titles can contain the word Usage. The default reverse walk reaches it in 47 elements, 29ms, since it sits at the end of the document beside the composer. The coordinate this replaces was (696, 938) and was already stale: the button measured (690,935 15x15) here, and it only ever landed while the window sat in its usual position and size. AXPress on an AXPopUpButton opens its popover. Logs one line per press to .claude/ax-press.log.
rules.description: Claude: ⇧⌘U → Usage (physical key i in Colemak)
Claude: ⌘B → ⌘. (Toggle Primary Sidebar)

rules.comment: Backslash is not remapped by Colemak, so no conversion is needed on either side.
rules.description: Claude: ⌥⌘B → ⌘\ (Toggle Secondary Sidebar)

rules.comment: Same Colemak bug as the Cmd+J rule (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/68859): the app re-translates Karabiner's output through the macOS Colemak input source, so to send the app Cmd+Shift+U we emit key_code i (Colemak maps the i-position to 'u'). Period is not remapped by Colemak, so the from side is used as-is.
rules.description: Claude: ⌘. → ⇧⌘U (Choose Model)
Claude: ⌘T → ⌃` (Toggle Terminal) (physical key f in Colemak)

rules.comment: Presses the primary Start button of the suggested-task chip (the card at the top right of a Code session that a spawn_task call puts up) through the accessibility tree. The card is a split button: an AXGroup described with the primary label holds an AXButton titled with it and, beside it, an AXPopUpButton described 'More start options'. The button's title is whatever the primary target is -- 'Start with worktree', 'Start locally', 'Start on <host>', 'Start on <host> with worktree', 'Send to cloud', 'Fix in this session' -- so the rule wildcards the label ({}) and qualifies by the sibling popup, which the card carries on every screen, and --role AXButton keeps it off that popup and off the wrapping group, which carries the same description. Only the head of the suggestion queue is rendered, so there is one match. Dry run: found in 311 elements, 30ms. Does nothing (found=false) when no chip is up, which is the app's own state and not a rule to guard. Logs one line per press to .claude/ax-press.log.
rules.description: Claude: ⇧⌘T → Start the suggested task (physical key f in Colemak)

rules.comment: Archives the current session by pressing the header's own overflow button and then its Archive item, both through the accessibility tree. The first command learns which chat is current from the session header, whose title button is labelled '<chat>, rename session' (--label-from), and AXPresses the AXPopUpButton described 'More options for <chat>' -- the three-dot button at the top right of the main pane (frame 706,42), which opens its dropdown. The second command polls the tree (--wait, every 25ms, up to the 2s budget) until an AXMenuItem titled 'Archive' exists and presses it, so a slow renderer delays the archive rather than misdirecting it, and a dropdown that never opens makes the second command time out with found=false and press nothing. The two go to the helper as one request joined with --then, because adjacent shell_commands in a to array collapse to the last one, and --then runs the second only if the first pressed: no menu, no press. This replaces the palette version (Cmd+K, type 'arch', Enter), whose Enter raced the palette's asynchronous Archive row and archived nothing under CPU load even at a measured-and-padded 150ms hold. Nothing here is timed. The first version of this rule opened the sidebar row's context menu with AXShowMenu, as the Cmd+Option+. rule does, with --first; that worked (3 of 3 idle, 3 of 3 with all 8 cores pegged, about 250ms end to end) but the header's button carries the same 'More options for <chat>' label, so with the sidebar hidden it became the first match and a right-click dispatched at it opened Electron's default Copy/Select All menu instead. Pressing the header button is what the mouse would do, needs no sidebar, and the search without --first walks from the end of the document and reaches it after about 140 elements: tested with the sidebar visible and hidden, both archived, 160-220ms end to end. The Archive item is pressed rather than typed as the menu's 'a' accelerator: a key_code after a shell_command can only be sequenced behind it with a fixed hold, which is the race being removed. Cmd+1 afterwards selects the first chat, as the old rule did, but it is posted by the helper (--key cmd+1, a CGEvent with its own modifier flags, so the still-held physical Cmd+Shift do not leak into it) rather than emitted by Karabiner. The helper posts it once the Archive item has left the tree, which is the dropdown closing and so the click having been handled -- 118-580ms after the press across 8 presses, longer when idle than under load, presumably the exit animation; if the item is still there when the budget runs out, nothing is posted and the log says gone=false. Digits are the same key in Colemak and QWERTY, so cmd+1 needs no conversion. Inspected in the Code tab only. Eight presses cannot tell 100% from 90%; ordinary use is the rest of the test. Logs one line per command to .claude/ax-press.log in the live checkout. Selecting the *next chat in the archived chat's own project* instead of Cmd+1 was built and then removed for cost: it needs an accessibility dump to learn the sidebar's order, which no label search can express, and a node process to read it, which was four helper launches against this rule's two while every call still launched the helper. Launches were the whole bill -- about 100ms each, of which the search was 10-50ms, because the helper re-spawns itself to disclaim responsibility -- so the successor version measured about 500ms against 160-220ms here, and Cmd+Option+. archived faster still at one launch plus the menu's own 'a'. Two things it found are worth keeping. Chat titles are not unique, so the sidebar cannot say which row is the current chat: two rows titled 'Test' in different projects sent the successor press to the wrong project's + button. What does say is the main pane's header, which carries an AXPopUpButton titled with the current chat's project beside the '<chat>, rename session' button. And archiving a project's last chat takes the whole group out of the sidebar, + button included, so there is nothing left to press afterwards: the app lands on its home screen, whose composer offers the last-used project. Selecting into the archived chat's project therefore has to happen before the archive, not after, which costs a third press and makes the archive go through the row rather than the header. The work is in git history (scripts/claude-archive-next.js, reverted here) if 200ms ever stops being the budget.
rules.description: Claude: ⇧⌘E → Archive Session via its ⋮ menu, then ⌘1 (physical key k in Colemak)

to.shell_command: printf '%s\0' com.anthropic.claudefordesktop "More options for {}" --role AXPopUpButton --label-from "{}, rename session" --log --then com.anthropic.claudefordesktop Archive --role AXMenuItem --wait --key cmd+1 --log | /usr/bin/nc -U "$HOME/.config/karabiner/scripts/bin/ax-press.sock"

rules.comment: Drives the app's own Go menu from the menu bar, because the Claude app ignores a native macOS App Shortcut override for these items (confirmed again when the rule was briefly removed: the App Shortcuts settings entry did nothing). fn+Ctrl+F2 focuses the menu bar, type-select on 'Go' highlights the menu title, Enter opens it, type-select on the item name highlights it and Enter activates it. The typed letters go through the macOS Colemak input source, so each is the physical key that types it: 'Go' is t, semicolon; 'Chat' is c, h, a, f; 'Code' is c, semicolon, g, k. No pauses: menu tracking runs a modal event loop that consumes the queue in order, so nothing races -- the previous sidebar-tab version of this rule passed 20 of 20 presses at 0ms after shipping with 150ms holds. The trailing vk_none keeps Enter from being the last `to` event, which would hold it down until the chord is released.
rules.description: Claude: ⇧⌘1 → Go to Chat; ⇧⌘2 → Go to Code

rules.comment: Opens the right-click menu of the chat shown in the main pane, from the keyboard. The app has no route to it otherwise: nothing in the Cmd+/ list opens it, the menu bar has no session items (so a macOS App Shortcut cannot reach it), and Chromium on macOS compiles out Shift+F10 (web_frame_widget_impl.cc: is_shift_f10 = false under IS_MAC), so the menu was mouse-only -- asked for in anthropics/claude-code#60551 and auto-closed. karabiner-config-ax-press (scripts/ax-press.swift) learns which chat is current from the session header, whose title button is labelled '<chat>, rename session' (--label-from), then performs AXShowMenu on the sidebar row's 'More options for <chat>' AXPopUpButton (--action), which makes Chromium dispatch at that element the contextmenu event a right-click would (browser_accessibility_cocoa.mm: SupportsShowMenuAction is true for every web node and PerformShowMenuAction calls ShowContextMenu). What opens is the menu the right-click opens, so its own keys then work: letters for Pin, Mark as unread, Rename and Delete, arrows into Add to project and Move to group, 1-9 inside them. --first because the sidebar is at the start of the document, so a forward walk reaches the row after the sidebar's ~200 elements rather than after the transcript. Needs the sidebar visible and the row rendered: a chat scrolled out of the list or in a collapsed group is not in the tree. Inspected in the Code tab only; the Chat tab's header was not checked. Two chats with the same title: the first in the sidebar wins. Measured: a contextmenu dispatched at the hover-revealed (opacity-0) More-options button does open the row's menu -- 3 presses, 3 menus, 57-78ms from the helper starting to the event landing, 497 elements visited, the button found again after the row moved between presses (frame y 707 to 738), and a title carrying an emoji prefix derived intact. Three presses cannot tell 100% from 90%; ordinary use is the rest of the test. Fallback if it ever stops opening: --action AXPress on the same button opens its dropdown instead. Logs one line per press to .claude/ax-press.log.
rules.description: Claude: ⌥⌘. → Chat Context Menu

to.shell_command: printf '%s\0' com.anthropic.claudefordesktop "More options for {}" --role AXPopUpButton --label-from "{}, rename session" --action AXShowMenu --first --log | /usr/bin/nc -U "$HOME/.config/karabiner/scripts/bin/ax-press.sock"

rules.comment: Opens the PR that the session's PR chip (the bar above the composer: '#<n>  <repo>  <branch>  +a -b  CI') links to, from the keyboard. The chip's number is an AXLink whose label is the PR number ('#5324'), so the rule matches it with the {} wildcard ('#{}' = any AXLink labelled '#' followed by something) and presses it; the default reverse walk finds the last such link in document order, which is the chip's, since the chip sits after the transcript and before the composer -- inline '#5324' links in the transcript come earlier and are skipped. Nothing else in the tree is an AXLink labelled '#...': the sidebar's PR rows are AXButtons ('#5336 · Open ...'). Needs a session with a PR chip; without one the helper reports found=false and nothing happens. AXPress on the link opens the PR in the default browser. Measured: 5 presses, 5 opens, 17-118ms from the helper starting to the press landing, 73-75 elements visited. Five presses cannot tell 100% from 90%; ordinary use is the rest of the test. Logs one line per press to .claude/ax-press.log.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+R → open the session's PR link (via accessibility) (physical key s in Colemak)
Quick Chars
Better Braces: Alt + O/I
Desktop Navigation: Right shift + brackets

rules.comment: Selects the last email in Shortwave's thread list, which the app has no shortcut of its own for -- its list bindings are J/K and the arrows, one row at a time. The list is virtualised: the tree holds the 33 rows the app has drawn rather than the whole mailbox, so --scroll-to-end scrolls the last row it can see into view and looks again, until the last row stops changing, and presses that one. Every row carries an avatar image labelled "Avatar for <sender>", the only label the rows share, and that label is also on the account avatar in the toolbar and on the avatars of an open thread, so --within keeps the search to the list column. The row itself is an unlabelled AXGroup six levels above the avatar, and the only element in that chain with an AXPress. This rule sits before "Launch apps" because that one takes right shift + t, the same physical key, and Karabiner runs the first manipulator that matches. Shift+G is also a capital G, so the rule emits the key itself and --unless-editing stands the press down while a text control has focus -- the composer, the search box, a label picker -- the same shape as the Settings sidebar keys below; without it every capital G typed in an email was swallowed and jumped the list instead. No --log, for the same reason as those keys: a line per capital G would bury the log.
rules.description: Shortwave: Shift+G → select the last email in the list (physical key t in Colemak)
Launch apps: Right shift + letters
Move italic to Cmd + Ctrl + I to make room for easy tab navigation
Tab Navigation: Cmd + H/I
GitHub notifications: Cmd + Option + T
em issues: Cmd + Ctrl + Option + E (physical key k in Colemak)
Chromium DevTools: Clear site data, focus page, and reload: Cmd + Option + R
Shortwave: Cmd+B → Cmd+/
Shortwave: Cmd+Option+B → Cmd+\

rules.comment: Presses the Always apply button in the toast Shortwave shows in the bottom-right corner after a label is applied, which promotes that one-off into a standing rule. The toast offers no keyboard shortcut, so it used to be reached by warping the pointer to (1272, 890) and clicking, which only landed while the Shortwave window sat in its usual position and size and left the cursor on the button. The button is in the accessibility tree as an AXButton titled "Always apply" (frame 1253,880 78x19, with an AXStaticText child of the same text), unique in the window, so karabiner-config-ax-press finds it by label: no coordinates, no pointer movement, nothing to restore. Shortwave is Electron and exposes its web content like any Chromium tree (1122-1450 elements, AXWebArea present), switched on by the helper's role read on the application object. The default reverse walk suits the target -- a forward dump reached it at element ~1128 of ~1200, so it sits near the end of the document. No --wait: the toast is already up when the shortcut is pressed, and a press with no toast reports found=false and does nothing. Observed live for 44 consecutive dumps (~45s) after one label application, so the toast outlasts the press by a wide margin. Logs one line per press to .claude/ax-press.log.
rules.description: Shortwave: Option+A → press Always apply on the label toast

rules.comment: Presses the Save button in Shortwave's settings dialogs, which the app gives no keyboard shortcut of its own for. Cmd+Enter is Shortwave's send shortcut everywhere else, so the rule must not swallow it: --else-key posts cmd+return from the helper itself whenever no Save button is on screen, which is what leaves compose and the inbox behaving as they always did. That fall-through is the whole cost of binding a key the app already uses -- a miss ends the search as soon as the walk shows the tree is populated (87ms over ~1000 elements), on top of the request to the resident helper. Nothing in the mail view carries the label at all, so the label alone tells the dialog from every other screen, and the dialog itself leaves only 65 elements in the tree -- Chromium drops the page behind a modal -- so the AXButton titled "Save" is reached after 19 of them, 27ms. Logs one line per press to .claude/ax-press.log, which here is one line per Cmd+Enter, sends included.
rules.description: Shortwave: Cmd+Enter → press Save in the settings dialog, or send as usual

rules.comment: Jumps to a section of Shortwave's Settings screen by pressing its sidebar row through the accessibility tree, on the bare key rather than a chord. Karabiner emits the key first and the helper runs behind it, so the character is never Karabiner's to give back: every other screen in the app types the digit or letter it always typed and keeps Shortwave's own single-key shortcuts, and the settings jump is whatever the helper finds afterwards. --else-key was the first shape tried, the one Cmd+Enter uses for Save above, and it did not survive being bound to typing keys -- the fall-through reported else_key_posted=true on every letter and not one of them reached the focused input, so the key was swallowed outright. Emitting it from the rule costs nothing and cannot miss. A row is an AXGroup (frame 27,y 134x25) carrying an AXPress, with the section name two levels below it in an AXStaticText whose AXValue is the label, so the rule matches the text and climbs with --ancestor '*:2' -- counting every level, because the wrapper in between is an anonymous AXGroup with no role to aim at. The default reverse walk suits the target: the sidebar is the last region in document order (elements 849-912 of 939), so it is reached before the thread pane, and the toolbar's own Compose button carries the same AXStaticText "Compose" earlier in the document, which a --first walk would find instead. --within is what keeps the fall-through honest for that one label -- the toolbar Compose sits at x=1364 and every sidebar row at x=33, so 4 types a 4 in the mail view rather than opening a draft -- and the rectangle is left open vertically so moving the window down does not break all fifteen at once. Nothing in the mail view carries any of the other fourteen labels (513 elements, none matched), so those fall through on the label alone. --unless-editing is what makes that safe: the sidebar rows are in the tree while a label picker's search box has focus too, so without it every letter typed there also jumped the sidebar. It reads the app's focused element and does nothing while that is a text control, which also makes typing the cheap path -- one attribute read, no walk. No --log, unlike every other ax-press rule here: these are typing keys, and a line per a-f keystroke would bury the log -- debug one with --dry-run from a shell instead. The cost is the one --else-key always has, paid here on every such keystroke rather than on a send: a request to the resident helper plus a full walk, the 57-98ms measured over ~1000 elements. 1-9 and A-F cover the fifteen sections of My account and the team; Support, Keyboard shortcuts and Experiments have no key left and are unbound. Colemak leaves the digits and A/B/C alone, D/E/F are physical g/k/e, and --else-key names keys by the same ANSI position, so each manipulator posts back exactly the key it took.
rules.description: Shortwave: 1-9, A-F → Settings sidebar sections, or the key itself (physical keys a b c g k e in Colemak for A-F)

rules.comment: Archives the top notification in the Inbox side panel by handing the whole gesture to a script, which moves the pointer there with real mouse events and clicks. Karabiner's own set_mouse_cursor_position warps the cursor without posting a mouse-moved event, and that is the root of every problem this rule has had: Chromium does not update its hover target from a warp, so the archive button, which only exists while the row is hovered, is either not armed or no longer armed when the click lands, and the click hit-tests against the row underneath and opens the notification instead. Waiting it out does not work reliably, because the window is bounded at both ends. Measured from the warp, with a single click: 60-80ms is too early and hits the row, 130ms archives, 250ms archives with false negatives, 400-500ms fails outright, and 150ms managed 1 in 4, so the window is narrow, drifts, and is not worth aiming at. An earlier two-click version appeared to work by firing at two offsets and landing one inside the window, which also means it archives twice whenever both land. The script sidesteps the window by walking the pointer in steps with CGEvents, which Chromium treats as genuine motion. Posting CGEvents needs Accessibility permission, which osascript does not have on its own, but Karabiner does and the processes it spawns inherit it; run the same command from a terminal and the events are silently filtered and the pointer never moves. It also clears the modifier flags on the click, since the physical Cmd+Shift are still down and an uncleared click arrives as Shift+Click and extends the text selection across the page, and it restores the cursor itself. Notion has no keyboard shortcut for archiving a single notification, so the mouse is the only route. Coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Notion window is top-left aligned at its usual size with the Inbox panel open; y is measured from the top of the first row rather than its middle, so it holds regardless of how tall the notification is, and the three buttons sit about 10 points apart, so shift x by 10 if the click lands on a neighbor.
rules.description: Notion: Cmd+Shift+E → click archive on top notification (166, 135) (physical key k in Colemak)

rules.comment: Opens the emoji picker for the last received message, so any emoji can be sent as a tapback without touching the mouse. The hover tapback bar is anchored to the message bubble, so it moves with the message's width and height and no fixed coordinate can reach its picker. The right-click menu is anchored to the click point instead, so the rule right-clicks a fixed point on the last message and works from there. (360, 890) sits inside the last received bubble whatever its size: received bubbles are left aligned at x 348 so a short message still covers x 360, and the transcript is bottom anchored so the bubble's lower edge stays at y 900 however tall the message is. A sent message is right aligned and will not be hit. move-to-tapback-picker.js then reads the menu's own window frame rather than assuming where it landed, because macOS pins the menu above the bottom of the screen and the height it pins from changes with the menu's items, so a message carrying a link would otherwise be off by the height of the extra ones; if no menu appears it leaves the pointer alone and the click lands back on the message. The right-click is held for 150ms rather than clicked instantly, which is what makes it reliable: the menu opens on the mouse down and starts a modal tracking loop, and an immediate mouse up can arrive before that loop is installed and dismiss it, which failed 5 times in 6 before the hold and 0 times in 6 after. Karabiner posts both clicks itself because it holds Accessibility and the osascript it spawns does not, which is also why the script only warps the pointer. The 200ms hold lets restore-mouse-position.js read the pointer before it moves, the 100ms hold keeps the right-click from racing the cursor move, and the 550ms hold covers osascript startup, measured at 70-110ms, plus the script's 250ms poll for the menu. Coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Messages window sits in its usual position and size with the conversation scrolled to the bottom; a group conversation indents received bubbles past x 360.
rules.description: Messages: Cmd+E → open the emoji picker for the last received message (physical key k in Colemak)

rules.comment: Copies the last response by pressing its Copy button through the accessibility tree rather than clicking it. The button sits beneath the response, so its position moves with the length of the response and of everything above it, and no fixed coordinate can reach it; the app offers no shortcut or menu item for it either (searched the bundle: 'Copy response' exists only as the button's tooltip, and the bindable-shortcut registry has no copy command). karabiner-config-ax-press (scripts/ax-press.swift) finds the last AXButton labelled 'Copy' in the focused window that has a 'Good response' sibling -- code-block copy buttons carry the same label, and the sibling is what tells the response's own button apart -- walking the document from its end so the search touches the composer and the last turn rather than the whole conversation (88 elements visited of 5297; 29-38ms from the helper starting to the press landing, over three presses), then AXPresses it: no pointer movement, no cursor restore. The window must be frontmost: the copy is a web clipboard write, which the page refuses when its document is not focused (pressed from a shell with another app in front, the button reported success and ChatGPT showed a 'couldn't copy' toast). Accessibility is granted to the helper itself rather than to Karabiner -- launchd runs it as its own responsible process, and a one-shot run from a shell re-spawns itself as one, so TCC judges the binary whoever started it, which is what made earlier spawned scripts' permissions unpredictable -- and the grant is keyed to the binary's path and its identifier-only designated requirement, so a rebuild keeps it (scripts/build-ax-press.sh). Because that grant would otherwise serve whatever process reaches the helper, it presses only when Karabiner-Console-User-Server is among the requesting process's ancestors; --dump and --dry-run work from a shell. Chromium exposes none of the page until an assistive client shows up, and what counts as showing up is asking the application object for its role (Chrome's and Electron's NSApplication subclasses both switch accessibility on there, following Apple's guidance for non-VoiceOver clients); the helper asks first thing, and a freshly launched instance that had ignored everything else for twenty minutes exposed its tree 124ms later, so the first press after ChatGPT relaunches should work too. While the tree is still only the window chrome the helper keeps looking for up to 2s, a budget sized for that first press on a long conversation rather than measured against one. If the newest turn is a user message, or the response is still streaming, the previous response's button is the last one and is pressed instead. Logs one line per press to .claude/ax-press.log.
rules.description: ChatGPT: Cmd+Shift+C → copy the last response (press its Copy button via accessibility)

rules.comment: Toggles the profile popup by clicking the sidebar footer's profile button at the position the accessibility tree reports. The button is the row at the bottom of the sidebar showing the avatar and account name; its aria-label, which Chromium puts in AXDescription, is 'Open profile menu' (app.asar, codex.profileFooter.openProfileMenu), and it is the trigger of a dropdown component like the composer's model picker, whose trigger AXPress could not open, so this rule clicks from the start: --click warps the pointer to the button's centre, posts a left click and warps it back. A second press while the popup is open clicks the same button, which the dropdown treats as a press outside its content and closes -- that is the toggle. When signed out the same button is labelled 'Open settings' and navigates to settings instead; the rule matches nothing then and does nothing. The default backwards walk reaches the footer in 186 elements of 476 (59-96ms in the dry run), against 308 forwards. The app binds nothing to Cmd+Shift+U (searched the bundle's command registry and ~/.codex/keybindings.json), so no --else-key. Logs one line per press to .claude/ax-press.log.
rules.description: ChatGPT: Cmd+Shift+U → toggle the profile popup (click the sidebar's profile button, found via accessibility; physical key i in Colemak)

rules.comment: Jumps to a section of Karabiner-Elements' own settings by selecting its sidebar row through the accessibility tree. The app offers no other route: its menu bar has only the standard App/Edit/View/Window/Help items (View holds nothing but Enter Full Screen), so a menu-bar sequence has nothing to type-select, and the sidebar's rows sit at coordinates that only hold while the window is where it was measured -- a settings window gets moved. The sidebar is an AXOutline described 'Sidebar' whose rows are AXRow/AXOutlineRow, each holding an AXImage (the SF Symbol, e.g. AXIdentifier 'gearshape') and an AXStaticText carrying the section name. SwiftUI puts that name in AXValue, which is why karabiner-config-ax-press reads AXValue as a label as well as AXDescription/AXTitle/AXHelp/AXIdentifier. The row itself is what selects, and it has no AXPress -- its only actions are AXShowDefaultUI and AXShowAlternateUI -- so the rule finds the static text, climbs to its AXRow (--ancestor) and sets AXSelected to true (--set), which is what navigates. --first because the sidebar is at the start of the window's tree, so the walk reaches the row without crossing the section pane. The four group headings (Modifications, Configurations, Maintenance, Diagnostic) are rows too, but they carry an AXHeading rather than a static text, so they are never matched. Cmd+1-9 and Cmd+0 cover the first ten sections in sidebar order; Uninstall, Expert, Quit-Restart, Log, System Extensions and Setup have no digit left and are unbound. Digits are the same key in Colemak and QWERTY, so nothing is converted here. Needs the settings window open: the app keeps running with its window closed, and with none the helper reports windows=0 and does nothing. Logs one line per press to .claude/ax-press.log.
rules.description: Karabiner-Elements: ⌘1-9, ⌘0 → settings sections (via accessibility)

to.shell_command: printf '%s\0' org.pqrs.Karabiner-Elements.Settings "Simple Modifications" --role AXStaticText --first --ancestor AXRow --set AXSelected=true --log | /usr/bin/nc -U "$HOME/.config/karabiner/scripts/bin/ax-press.sock"

printf '%s\0' org.pqrs.Karabiner-Elements.Settings "Function Keys" --role AXStaticText --first --ancestor AXRow --set AXSelected=true --log | /usr/bin/nc -U "$HOME/.config/karabiner/scripts/bin/ax-press.sock"

printf '%s\0' org.pqrs.Karabiner-Elements.Settings "Complex Modifications" --role AXStaticText --first --ancestor AXRow --set AXSelected=true --log | /usr/bin/nc -U "$HOME/.config/karabiner/scripts/bin/ax-press.sock"

printf '%s\0' org.pqrs.Karabiner-Elements.Settings "Virtual Keyboard" --role AXStaticText --first --ancestor AXRow --set AXSelected=true --log | /usr/bin/nc -U "$HOME/.config/karabiner/scripts/bin/ax-press.sock"

rules.comment: Calendar's own resize and nudge chords are Ctrl+Shift+arrow and Ctrl+arrow; they are handled by the calendar view, not a menu item, so there is nothing for a menu-bar sequence to type-select. The 100ms hold on the arrow is earned: at 0ms the remapped chord landed 4-5 times in 10 while the same chord pressed directly landed 10/10, and nothing else happened on a miss -- so Calendar reads the modifier state after the key-down, and Karabiner releasing Control right behind the arrow loses the race that a physical press never runs. Floor search, 10 presses per value: 25ms 8/10, 40ms failed, 60ms 10/10, 80ms 10/10, 100ms 10/10. Shipped at 75 for headroom over the ~50ms floor (see docs/pauses.md on floors versus shipped values). The vi-mode rule at the top of this file carries Calendar-scoped copies of these four chords, because Karabiner does not run one manipulator's output through later rules: the arrow vi mode emits for d+j / d+k never reaches this rule.
rules.description: Calendar: Shift+Up/Down → Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down (resize event); Cmd+Up/Down → Ctrl+Up/Down (nudge event)
